company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates with $56.05 vs. the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex more aggressively in the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS solidly at 53 cents vs. the Street's 36 cents, and importantly the beat holds even excluding tariff refunds — stripping out the 11-cent tailwind still yields 42 cents vs. the 36-cent consensus. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly but EPS guidance was left unchanged, and the FQ2 EPS midpoint of 46 cents is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings significant large-cap CFO experience, having previously served in that role at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The appointment is a straightforward leadership transition with no financial guidance changes attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS at 78 cents vs. the Street's 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% — well below the Street's 13.85% estimate — despite revenue coming in slightly above estimates at $2.311 billion. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures squeezing household budgets and keeping retail soft, with increasing material costs pressuring margins. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a ~75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive Phase trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in participants. The results mark a meaningful clinical milestone for the company's obesity drug pipeline and put VK2735 among the more effective weight loss efficacy readouts in the GLP-1 space. The data-driven spike reflects significant investor enthusiasm for the program.

sectors: The RV sector faces ongoing macro headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation are keeping retail soft. The GLP-1/obesity drug space gets a fresh positive datapoint from Viking's VK2735 results. Robotics and Physical AI perception is in focus with Cognex's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday, September 22nd, covering six names reporting before the open. No broad macro or Fed commentary in this note — let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The company beat fourth fiscal quarter earnings at $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the quality of that beat is questionable. Roughly 250 basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the picture gets less flattering — domestic comps came in at just plus 1.6% versus the Street's expectation of plus 3.1%, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did flag improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well-positioned for fiscal 2027 growth. Call this one mixed — a beat, but not a clean one.

Cognex is acquiring RealSense — the depth-sensing camera and vision technology leader for robotics and Physical AI applications — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to do $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a clear strategic move into the Physical AI and robotic perception space. Bullish for the stock.

MillerKnoll is the cleanest beat in this group. First fiscal quarter EPS came in at 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, the company still beats at 42 cents. Sales missed — down 3.3% organically to $923 million versus the $943 million consensus — but orders were up 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year sales guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance is unchanged and the second quarter EPS midpoint is in line with the Street. This is a genuine beat with real operating leverage.

THOR Industries missed. Fourth fiscal quarter EPS came in at 78 cents versus the 87-cent estimate. Gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well short of the Street's 13.85% estimate. Management called out stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation as ongoing retail headwinds. No formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. There are some bright spots — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — but the headline numbers and qualitative tone were cautious. Bearish near-term.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1st. Hau previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Standard leadership transition — no financial guidance changes.

And the most exciting name this morning: Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss. That is a strong efficacy readout and puts VK2735 in serious contention in the obesity drug race. Clearly bullish.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the momentum trade, MillerKnoll is the quiet fundamental beat, AutoZone's beat needs scrutiny, and THOR reflects a tough consumer macro for big-ticket discretionary spending. Stay focused.
